n: The only psalm in Book Three credited to David. It is woven from phrases found elsewhere in scripture, like a prayer built from beloved lines. David begins by asking God to bend down and listen, for he is poor and needy.
Protect my life, for I am devoted to you. “Holy” here means faithful and loyal, not sinless.

f.g: Hebrew ḥasid — devoted, faithful, a covenant-keeper.

n: Be gracious to me, Lord, because I call to you all day long.
Make your servant glad, for I lift my soul to you.

f.w: unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul

n: Here is why he can pray with confidence: God is good, quick to forgive, and overflowing with loyal love toward all who call on him.
Listen to my prayer, Lord, and pay attention to my pleas.
In trouble he will call, because he is confident God will answer.
No so-called god compares to the Lord, and no works match his.

f.w: Among the gods there is none like unto thee

n: All the nations God made will come and bow before him and honor his name — a vision of worldwide worship.

f.w: All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship

n: For he is great, does wonders, and is God alone.
A beautiful prayer: teach me your way so I can walk in your truth; unite my heart — gather my scattered loyalties into one — to reverence you.
With his whole heart he will praise God and honor his name forever. A united heart can praise wholeheartedly.
God’s love for him is great — he has rescued him from the depths of the grave.

f.g: The depths of Sheol — the realm of the dead; near death.

n: Arrogant and violent men have risen against him, seeking his life with no regard for God.

f.w: have not set thee before them

n: But God is the opposite of these violent men: compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love and faithfulness. This quotes God’s self-description to Moses on Sinai.

f.w: a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering

n: Turn to me and be gracious; give your strength to your servant and save the son of your maidservant — one born into your household and service.

f.g: A servant born in the household — one who belongs to God from birth.

n: He asks for a sign of God’s favor, so his enemies will see that the Lord has helped and comforted him — and be ashamed.

f.g: A sign of your goodness and favor.
